source.title: Is the Information Bottleneck Robust Enough? Towards Label-Noise Resistant Information Bottleneck Learning
source.authors: Yi Huang; Qing-Yun Sun; Yi-Sen Gao; Hao-Nan Yuan; Xingcheng Fu; Jian-Xin Li

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices. Some figure text is garbled, and figure values are not reliably readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies label-noise conditions and reports model accuracy during training and on test data. This bears on V4's noisy-label behavior, but it does not test completely random labels, chance test error, or the original claim's full setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own label-noise experiments. Preliminary results in Figures E.1 and E.2 are included below. Other accuracy tables compare methods under noisy labels but do not report the train-set fitting behavior needed for V4. Cited claims about clean samples being learned earlier are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The preliminary experiments examine noisy-label fitting and generalization in information-bottleneck networks, a new setting bearing on V4. Appendix E.3 explicitly reports GIB fitting noisy labels while test performance declines, and reports VIB training collapse. They do not establish perfect training fit across noise rates.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify vulnerability of standard IB methods to label noise and conclude that LaT-IB's representation disentanglement and three-phase training improve robustness while preserving minimally sufficient representations.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies label noise in IB image and graph classification experiments; it does not reproduce the original random-label intervention or its training-error and test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-noise type and rate; the paper describes VIB's decline as more pronounced at higher noise and reports collapse under extreme noise. Figure E.2 varies graph label-noise rate.

fits_no_version.finding: In Appendix E.7, LaT-IB's encoder T gradually fits all noisy training data, while encoder S reaches about 65% training accuracy on Cora with 40% uniform noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A purpose-built disentanglement and sample-selection procedure can produce different noisy-label fitting behavior in its two encoders. This does not independently establish spontaneous clean-first learning in standard networks.

fits_no_version.finding: LaT-IB improves classification accuracy under noisy supervision and adversarial attacks; timing tables compare its computational cost with other methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LaT-IB improves robustness and efficiency relative to selected IB baselines. These method comparisons do not establish random-label memorization or its optimization cost.

record.problems: For the preliminary results relevant to noisy-label learning, key values are figure-only and the supplied figure text is garbled. The reported sweeps do not cover all labels corrupted. The text does not state that train accuracy is perfect across the tested noise conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2–4 and E.3–E.5 report separate test accuracies for methods under noisy labels, but do not report training-set fitting; excluded because they cannot establish the behavior in V4. Figures E.1–E.3 are figure-only; no reliable numeric values can be assigned from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels, and convergence time across corruption fractions. The reported timing tables compare methods instead.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a zero-to-complete corruption sweep and test performance approaching chance. The preliminary GIB prose establishes qualitative noisy-label fitting and declining test performance, without recoverable training endpoints.
The necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation for random-label fitting and true-label generalization.

Direct comparison of learning clean versus corrupted examples over time. GIB's early test improvement followed by deterioration is consistent with this account but does not separately measure the two learning trajectories; the explicit clean-first claim is attributed to prior work.

missing.what: The explicit statement that VIB fails to train at β = 0.01 with 50% symmetric noise should be recorded as a qualitative training-failure result. Table 1 additionally reports 10.0% classification accuracy for VIB versus 79.4% for ResNet34 in that condition; this accuracy alone must not be treated as training accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Figures E.1–E.3 are already declared in rows_left_out, so their omitted results are not added to missing. Appendix E.3 nevertheless supplies usable qualitative evidence: GIB gradually fits noisy labels as test performance declines, with deterioration worsening at higher noise. This supports that component of V4 but does not establish the version's perfect-fit requirement. LaT-IB's intentionally differentiated encoder behavior is not evidence against V4.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling experiment or test error at chance.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or convergence time by corrupted-label fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The figures show results only up to specified noisy-label settings, not from none to all corrupted labels. The paper does not establish perfect training accuracy at every noise rate or report the required full sweep in recoverable numeric form.
No experiment tests whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

The paper cites prior work about clean samples being fit earlier and describes clean/noisy encoder behavior, but it does not compare learning of true labels with learning of completely random labels over training.

relationships.condition: VIB with compression coefficient β = 0.01 on CIFAR-10 with 50% symmetric label noise
relationships.reason: Based on the text rather than extracted rows: Section 5.5 explicitly says VIB fails to train in this condition, and Appendix E.3 reports training collapse. Thus continued perfect fitting under increasing label noise does not extend unconditionally to this IB objective.
relationships.display_finding: Training collapsed rather than fitting the noisy training set.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
